purpose: Score independent restoration/conservation systems against the same empirical CREST motif without treating them as proof of the finite theorem.

cases.action: remove migration barrier / restore longitudinal passage
evidence_basis: Two Elwha dams blocked access to more than 90% of the watershed before removal.
Post-removal eDNA used 11 species-specific assays and found species-specific recolonization timing and spatial extent.
Focal passage/detection targets are reportable without full community-state identification.
A 440-study review identifies persistent soil microbial, nutrient, seed-bank, secondary-invasion and reinvasion legacies after invasive control.
A 2023 systematic review reports reinvasion and/or secondary invasion in more than 35% of reviewed studies while seed-bank response was rarely examined.
Invader-control success can therefore be reportable while native-community recovery remains unresolved.
After 7-16 years of rewetting, methanogen abundance and composition can approach pristine conditions while methane-production activity remains substrate-limited.
Large-scale tropical rewetting can reduce subsidence while vegetation recovery remains a distinct restoration dimension.
Hydrological restoration is therefore a reportable target that does not uniquely identify carbon-cycle or microbial recovery state.

cases.action: reintroduce prescribed fire after long exclusion
cases.partial_reason: The action/history/seed-bank response pieces are strongly supported, but the evidence-state versus reportable-target separation is assembled across studies rather than demonstrated as one integrated monitoring experiment.
evidence_basis: Fire reintroduction after long exclusion can cause novel tree mortality because accumulated duff/fuel structure changes response.
Prescribed-fire effects on seed banks can differ from visible above-ground community response.
Ecological condition and fire season can alter seed-bank response.

summary.primary_conclusion: The qualitative CREST motif recurs independently in freshwater restoration, invasion management, and peatland restoration, with prescribed fire providing a strong partial replication. The repeated phenomenon is not generic response heterogeneity; it is intervention-induced representational refinement with possible monitoring insufficiency and target/state separation.
summary.theorem_firewall: No empirical case establishes the arbitrary-m finite no-bound theorem.
